description: Create a minimal README for informal projects

action.recommendation: Create a minimal README.md with: project name, one-sentence description, how to install/run, and contact information. Even for informal projects, a README helps others (and future you) understand the project's purpose.

rationale: A minimal README is the lowest barrier to entry for project documentation and is valuable even for personal projects.

action.recommendation: Document non-obvious code with inline comments. Focus on: why decisions were made (not what the code does), complex algorithms, workarounds and their context, and deprecated code with migration guidance. Avoid noise comments that restate the code.

rationale: Inline comments document intent that code alone cannot express. They are the primary documentation for many codebases.

action.recommendation: Use Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) to document significant technical decisions. Each ADR should include: context, decision, status, and consequences. Store in /docs/adr/ and reference ADRs in code comments where relevant. Use MADR or Nygard format.

rationale: ADRs preserve the context behind architectural decisions, preventing future teams from repeating mistakes or reversing decisions for undocumented reasons.

action.recommendation: Create and maintain an ADR template to ensure consistency across decisions. Include sections for: title, date, status (proposed/accepted/deprecated/superseded), context, decision, and consequences. Link superseding ADRs to their predecessors.

rationale: Consistent ADR format makes them easier to discover, read, and navigate as the collection grows.

action.recommendation: Create operational runbooks for all production services. Each runbook must include: service overview, architecture diagram, deployment procedure, common failure modes with resolution steps, on-call contacts, and escalation paths. Test runbooks by following them in dry-run exercises.

rationale: Operational runbooks reduce MTTR during incidents and enable on-call rotation without single-person knowledge concentration.

description: Standardise runbook format across the organisation

action.recommendation: Adopt a standard runbook format across all teams. Include: last-reviewed date, service owner, severity classification, pre-requisites, step-by-step procedures with expected outputs, and rollback steps. Review and update all runbooks after incidents.

rationale: Standardised runbooks reduce cognitive load during incidents when engineers are under pressure.

action.recommendation: Implement comprehensive audit trail documentation. Document: all significant decisions with approvals, change history with rationale, compliance evidence artefacts, security review records, and release approval chains. Ensure audit records are tamper-evident and retained per compliance requirements.

rationale: Full audit trails are required for regulated industries and provide evidence of due diligence for governance purposes.

description: Maintain a structured CHANGELOG for releases

action.recommendation: Maintain a CHANGELOG.md following Keep a Changelog format (keepachangelog.com). Document Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed/Security sections for each release. Automate changelog generation from conventional commits where possible.

rationale: A structured CHANGELOG communicates changes to users and stakeholders, and provides an audit trail of what changed and why.
